title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892 — herbarium denominator and evidence bounds
problem: The minimum Tempe packet currently contains nine independently indexed Ganong-Blaschka sheets and only Hoffmannseggia has a secure later model descendant. That pattern is analytically useful but cannot yet be converted into a percentage or expedition-wide model-conversion rate.

institutional_bounds.harvard_finding_aid: Harvard's Blaschka/Ware finding aid reports more than 300 herbarium specimens collected by Rudolf and Harvard-affiliated botanists during the 1892 and 1895 visits combined, and says these specimens remained in the Harvard University Herbaria.
institutional_bounds.year_problem: The >300 figure combines 1892 and 1895 and cannot serve as a denominator for 1892 without item-level separation.
institutional_bounds.database_problem: The public HUH specimen database is a digitized/indexed view into a larger and evolving physical collection. Search absence is therefore not historical absence.

denominators.name: current discovered/indexed packet
denominators.definition: The nine Tempe sheets surfaced in the present search and independently verified in HUH metadata.
denominators.use: Qualitative microhistory of branching, repeated sampling and secure/uncertain descendant links.
denominators.prohibition: Do not call this the complete Tempe collection or use 1/9 as a conversion rate.

denominators.name: complete 1892 Ganong-Blaschka herbarium subset
denominators.definition: All HUH sheets attributable to W. F. Ganong & R. Blaschka in 1892, separated by date/locality and historical/accepted taxonomy.
denominators.status: not yet recovered as a complete export/query result
denominators.use: Once bounded, can support locality-level retention analysis and systematic specimen/model crosswalks.

denominators.name: all 1892 expedition reference outputs
denominators.definition: Drawings, dried specimens, alcohol-preserved material, seeds, bulbs, living plants, detached fresh material and other documented reference media produced by Rudolf, Ganong, Cameron and local collaborators.
denominators.status: heterogeneous and not yet enumerable as one closed corpus
denominators.use: Necessary denominator for any broad claim about how field reference production was later reactivated in glass.

negative_evidence_rules: No current HUH hit does not mean no historical specimen existed.
No exact species-string model hit does not mean no glass descendant existed; historical synonymy and label changes must be checked.
A same-genus model is not a descendant without species-level or documentary linkage.
A specimen/model metadata match does not prove the surviving sheet was the sole physical template used in the workshop.
More than 300 specimens across 1892+1895 is not an 1892 count.
Conversion-rate language is prohibited until the relevant denominator is explicitly bounded.
what_the_nine_sheet_packet_does_prove: A tightly dated Tempe collecting episode generated multiple retained herbarium references.
The same taxon, Eriogonum inflatum, was sampled on adjacent days, showing repeated sampling rather than a one-row species checklist.
Hoffmannseggia provides a secure metadata-level branch from field specimen to later model 433.
Several other discovered sheets currently lack secure model descendants, demonstrating that the archival branches are non-identical even if later synonym work changes individual classifications.
what_it_does_not_prove: that only one of nine Tempe references was modelled
that all nine sheets represent everything collected at Tempe
that the herbarium corpus exhausts the field reference stock
that absent exact-string matches are true historical negatives
next_retrievals: Obtain a collector-level HUH export/search result for W. F. Ganong & R. Blaschka, year 1892, including barcode, historical name, accepted name, locality, date and image link.
If public search cannot enumerate the full set reliably, request a database export or staff-assisted query from HUH.
Separate 1892 and 1895 within the >300-specimen finding-aid aggregate.
Crosswalk every recovered 1892 sheet through historical synonyms against Harvard model labels and shipment lists.
Keep drawings/living material/preserved material as separate media ledgers before any attempt at expedition-wide conversion analysis.
article_use: The source-critical contribution is stronger if the paper displays bounded evidence and missing denominators explicitly. Selective conversion is currently an event-level mechanism, not a measured expedition-wide rate.
